propositions: A transient GitHub git fetch hang exceeding _GIT_TIMEOUT=300s converts to SnapshotFetchError, which the adapter's blanket exception handler converts to a BLOCK decision with review-error reason, resulting in a spurious LLM-Review -1 vote

The spurious -1 vote prevents backfill reconciliation from re-reviewing the change because reconcile.py pre-filters on already_voted and has_llm_review_vote, removing vote-less changes from the retry pool

The inner adapter exception handler lacks distinction between retryable infrastructure faults and genuine review conclusions, routing all exceptions to fail-closed voting instead of the no-vote path that upper layers (app.py, reconcile.py) already implement for hung reviews

The fix adds a _is_retryable_infra classifier to catch SnapshotFetchError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, and ConnectionError, routing them to an ABSTAIN decision that posts no vote and writes no dedup row
An ABSTAIN result in the voter emits a VOTER_ERROR marker and returns status=abstained without posting a vote, leaving the change eligible for backfill re-review on the next pass
The fix ensures retryable infrastructure faults do not create durable blocking votes that suppress their own safety-net recovery
